newsitem.title: CANADA: Feed barley price stabilizes on Saudi demand - CWB.
newsitem.headline: Feed barley price stabilizes on Saudi demand - CWB.

text.p: World feed barley prices stabilized in the last month on firm Saudi Arabian import demand, a Canadian Wheat Board market analyst said.

"Feed barley prices have stabilized in the past month primarily due to some very strong demand from Saudi Arabia. They're projected to import about five million tonnes of barley which would account for 50 percent of world feed barley trade. That's up quite a bit from last year," CWB analyst Larry Sawatzky said.

The CWB on Thursday left its world feed barley price forecast unchanged at the C$140-C$160 a tonne range.
Some industry participants expected a slight decline from last month's range.

"Malting barley prices are the only ones that are down and we lowered them because Australia's crop quality prospects look very good and they're expecting very high selection rates, so their exportable supplies of malting barley should be higher than earlier expectations," Sawatzky added.
The CWB on Thursday lowered its world malt barley price forecast by C$3 a tonne.
Special Select Canada Western Two-Row barley was lowered to the C$217-C$237-a-tonne range from C$220-C$240 in November.
SSCW Six-Row barley was lowered to the C$177-C$197 a tonne range from C$180-C$200 in-store Vancouver or St. Lawrence.
